parts.title: A mountain planted on purpose
parts.intro: Smokvica Krmpotska and Krivi Put were settled on purpose, by refugees the Habsburgs planted on an empty mountain to hold it. With one exception, every place in this archive before 1884 lies within a day's walk of the Velebit. These chapters are the Bunjevci and the Frontier, Senj and Karlobag, the map, and the names the registers wrote the family under.

parts.title: Four families, and the lines under them
parts.intro: The archive follows four surnames with a page each, Blažević, Žubrinić, Papić and Prpić, while the descent runs through more than twenty. The drawn line comes first and then each family in turn, with the names of Selce, Otočac and Karlobag that the direct line carries. The registers take the line back to about 1717, in four parishes, and no further.

parts.title: A port, a war, and the Highveld
parts.intro: Hedviga was born in a dying port on the Adriatic and died seventy-five years later on the Highveld, having crossed a world war, a country that stopped existing, and two continents. These chapters hold her life and her mother's, the town in 1943, the papers and pictures that survive, and the work that took others of the family to Port Pirie and to America.
